design_concept.name: Stone & Reed
design_concept.style_summary: A deeper, more grounded Wabi Sabi expression. Charcoal clay plaster feature walls ground each space while warm oatmeal, undyed linen, and aged ash timber soften the mood. Reed screens and washi pendant lamps diffuse light gently. Minimal furniture — every piece chosen for its tactile honesty and quiet permanence.
colour_palette: Charcoal clay / dark ash plaster — feature walls
Warm oatmeal / undyed cream — upholstery and bedding
material_palette: Vinyl plank flooring — warm pale ash tone
Aged ash timber veneer — carpentry and furniture frames
Charcoal clay plaster paint — feature walls (living, master bedroom)
Matte warm grey laminate — kitchen cabinets
Dark sintered stone / slate-look — kitchen countertop
Natural undyed linen — sofa, curtains, bedding
Rattan weave — dining chairs, pendants, side tables
Reed / bamboo slat panel — living TV wall, bedroom headboard wall
Natural rope — pendant fittings and detail trim
lighting_strategy: Cove lighting behind reed slat panel in living
Washi paper and rattan pendant over dining table
Bedside wall-mount rattan pendants — master bedroom
No cool white or blue-tinted lights
design_concept.budget_strategy: Focus budget on charcoal clay plaster feature walls ($4k), aged ash carpentry (kitchen, wardrobes, TV unit), and quality linen soft furnishings. Loose furniture is mid-tier — solid ash or rattan, no mass-market flat-pack look. Keep lighting handmade-style washi pendants to reinforce Wabi Sabi feel without high cost.

rooms.design_intent: Open-plan living and dining unified by pale ash vinyl flooring and charcoal clay plaster on the TV feature wall. Reed slat panel frames the TV console with warm cove lighting behind. Linen sofa faces the feature wall. Dining zone anchored by a raw ash table and rattan chairs under a washi rope pendant.
clearance_notes: Sofa-to-TV wall clearance approximately 3200mm — sufficient for family seating
Dining chair pull-out zone approximately 900mm behind chairs — confirmed adequate
Main circulation aisle from entry to bedrooms kept clear at 900mm+
uncertainties: Exact position of structural column at entry — assumed clear of sofa zone

rooms.design_intent: Open kitchen with dark slate-look sintered stone countertop on warm grey matte laminate cabinets. Reed-wrapped overhead shelving replaces upper cabinets to keep the space airy. Bomb shelter door painted warm grey to blend with cabinetry — visually recessed, functionally accessible.
clearance_notes: Bomb shelter door swing must remain unobstructed — no cabinetry in front
uncertainties: Exact kitchen width not confirmed from visible dimensions — base cabinets proposed at 600D standard

rooms.design_intent: Serene retreat in charcoal clay plaster on the headboard wall, with undyed linen bedding on an aged ash platform bed. Reed slat panel headboard feature. Slim ash wardrobe runs the full wall opposite. Bedside rattan pendant lamps replace table lamps to preserve surface calm.
clearance_notes: Bed side clearance approximately 700mm both sides — adequate
Wardrobe front clearance approximately 1000mm — confirmed adequate

rooms.design_intent: Child's bedroom with ash loft bed (bunk + desk below). Wardrobe along west wall. Textured warm grey plaster on one wall. Jute rug and cotton play mat on floor.
clearance_notes: Loft bed guardrail at 400mm above mattress — confirmed safe for children

rooms.design_intent: Second child's bedroom — wider room (5200mm). Same ash loft bed concept, mirrored layout. Two north-facing windows bring soft filtered daylight. Warm grey plaster feature wall behind the loft bed.
